title: A Benford's law based method for fraud detection using R Library
author: Azevedo, Gonçalves, et al.
materials: P0 is the expected frequency under Benford´s law.
n is the number of records.

steps.title: Install software and packages
steps.instruction: Install RStudio Desktop version 1.2.1335 on Windows 10 Home (version 10.0.183363) on a notebook with Intel Core i7 1.8 GHz (8th gen) and 8 GB RAM; install R and the CRAN package benford.analysis; clone the GitHub repository https://github.com/cazevedo1977/brazilian-welfareprogram-bolsafamilia-dataanalysis to obtain the two analysis scripts.

steps.title: Download raw withdrawal data
steps.instruction: On May 10 2020 download the Bolsa Família withdrawal CSV files for January and March of 2018 and 2019 from http://www.portaltransparencia.gov.br/download-de-dados/bolsa-familia-saques (select year/month and click “Baixar”). Files are semicolon‑separated CSV encoded Latin‑1; keep original names such as 201801_BolsaFamilia_Saques.csv. Also download the pre‑aggregated municipal files (BolsaFamilia_Municipalities_Jan_2018.csv, BolsaFamilia_Municipalities_Mar_2018.csv, BolsaFamilia_Municipalities_Jan_2019.csv, BolsaFamilia_Municipalities_Mar_2019.csv) from https://www.kaggle.com/caioazevedo/brazilian-welfareprogram-bolsafamilia-dataanalysis.

steps.title: Set working directory and read raw file
steps.instruction: Open RStudio, set the working directory to the folder containing the CSV files, e.g. setwd("C:/Users/cazev/OneDrive/Desktop/docs/Mestrado/paper benford law/references/datasources"); then read the raw withdrawal file with read.csv2(file="201801_BolsaFamilia_Saques.csv", sep=';', header=TRUE, fileEncoding="latin1").

steps.title: Run first‑approach Benford test on raw data
steps.instruction: Source and run the script Benford_BolsaFamilia_MethodsX.FirstApproach.R. The script analyses the variable VALOR.PARCELA (withdrawal value) using Z‑statistic, chi‑square and MAD. Record that the dataset contains 13,442,529 records. The observed chi‑square for first‑digit is 6,480,128.958, which exceeds the 5 % critical value 15.507, so the first‑digit test fails; first‑two‑digit chi‑square is not computed because the first‑digit test already failed.

steps.title: Group data by municipalities
steps.instruction: In the same script, after the failed test, execute dataSet <- myGroupDataByMunicipalities(dataSet, "BolsaFamilia_Municipalities_Jan_2018.csv") to create a new CSV where each row corresponds to a municipality and the column “Withdrawal value” contains the total amount paid by that municipality.

steps.title: Run final Benford analysis on aggregated data
steps.instruction: Open and run Benford_BolsaFamilia_MethosdsX.FinalAnalysis.R (ensure the working directory points to the municipal CSV files). The script computes Z‑statistic, chi‑square and MAD for both first‑digit and first‑two‑digit distributions of municipal withdrawal totals.

steps.title: Compare results with statistical thresholds
steps.instruction: Use the following 5 % significance thresholds: Z‑statistic critical value 1.96 (also 2.57 for 1 % and 1.64 for 10 %); chi‑square critical values 15.507 for first‑digit and 112.022 for first‑two‑digit (89 degrees of freedom); MAD critical ranges – first digits: 0.000‑0.006 close, 0.006‑0.012 acceptable, 0.012‑0.015 marginally acceptable, >0.015 non‑conformity; first‑two digits: 0.000‑0.012 close, 0.012‑0.018 acceptable, 0.018‑0.022 marginally acceptable, >0.022 non‑conformity. The observed MAD = 0.0010 (below the 0.0022 limit). Aggregated chi‑square results are 11.932 (first‑digit) < 15.507 and 80.8485 (first‑two‑digit) < 112.022. Four Z‑statistics exceed 1.96: digit 48 (2.6486), 35 (2.3590), 17 (2.0468) and 34 (1.9683), which is within the expected 4‑5 spikes at a 5 % level.

steps.title: Perform summation test
steps.instruction: Apply the summation test to the first‑two‑digit groups of the aggregated data. The theoretical proportion for each group is 1/90 = 0.011; with a 25 % upper tolerance the critical proportion is 0.01375. Identify all digit groups whose sum‑proportion exceeds 0.01375.

steps.title: Select top digit groups and export municipalities
steps.instruction: Rank digit groups by their sum‑proportion and select the ten highest (example from Table 4: digit 10 – 23 434 municipalities – total BRL 109,877,366 – proportion 0.0456; digit 12 – 34 311 municipalities – total BRL 104,132,939 – proportion 0.0433; … digit 66 – 55 185 municipalities – total BRL 66,550,185 – proportion 0.0276). Use the final line of the script to write the list of municipalities belonging to those groups to a CSV file for further audit. Optionally merge this file with population data from IBGE for additional fraud‑risk assessment.

description: Every statistical analysis lay down whether results have statistical significance according to pre-established limits. Significance levels show how likely a pattern in your data is due to chance. The significance level, also denoted as alpha or α, is the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true. The most common level used to mean something is good enough to be believed is 95%. Thus, a significance level of 95% indicates a 5% risk of concluding that a difference exists when there is no actual difference. [1] Source: Decree No. 5.209, of 17 September 2004, regulates Law No. 10.836, which creates the Bolsa Família programme and sets out other provisions, http://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_Ato2004-2006/2004/Decreto/D5209.htm (accessed on June 22, 2019).
